title: Build ellipsoids from a block with a sphere mesh, not a Ball part
observation: Storm clouds and fog built as Ball parts with flat sizes (for example 1.7 x 0.55 x 1.7 of a base size) kept that Size property but were drawn as small spheres, so a cloud bank read as scattered dark balls from a boat. Rebuilding each puff as a block with a SpecialMesh of type Sphere drew the intended flat ellipsoid at the same Size. Separately, overlapping see-through ellipsoids showed each other's insides and read as soap bubbles; opaque billows read as solid cartoon clouds.
recommendation: For any squashed round shape (clouds, domes, skulls, pebbles, canopies), use a Block part with a SpecialMesh MeshType Sphere and check it in a screenshot. Make clouds that should look solid opaque; keep transparency for fog that should be seen through.
applies_when: Making clouds, domes or organic shapes from primitive parts
A Ball part looks smaller or rounder than its Size suggests
limits: Observed in one place in Roblox Studio in October 2026
Collision and ray behaviour of mesh ellipsoids were not studied (the clouds are non-colliding)

evidence.detail: Sections 17 and 23, with the before-storm and after-storm-clouds screenshots: V9's Ball puffs against V10's opaque sphere-mesh billows.
